_doc.signal_labels: neutral = BULLISH SIGNAL / BEARISH SIGNAL / NO EDGE; directional = BUY / SELL / HOLD style. The only switch for wording (decision 3). The mandatory disclaimer shows in both modes.
_doc.primary_horizon_d: horizon used for the headline signal
_doc.universe: min_adv_inr_cr = minimum 20-day average traded value in Rs crore; min_history_d = minimum daily bars; exclude = boards/types left out
_doc.costs: per leg, in basis points of traded value (1 bp = 0.01%). Statutory rates as of 2026 (NSE cash/F&O, SEBI, GST, stamp); check against the broker contract note before relying on them. slippage_bps_by_adv_decile: index 0 = most liquid decile, 9 = least liquid, per leg.
_doc.eval: expanding walk-forward; test_d block length; purge_d + embargo_d between train and test; min_trades_oos per strategy; fdr_q Benjamini-Hochberg level; n_boot bootstrap resamples; data_start/first_test = first data year used and first out-of-sample block; select_lookback_d = recent window (days) the selection statistics use, so a decayed edge can be seen to decay; boot_block = mean block length (trades) of the stationary bootstrap; boot_prelim_p = bootstrap is run only for pairs whose quick t-test p is below this (others keep the t-test p, which can never be significant after FDR); stab_* = yearly-block stability rule; plateau_min_trades = minimum trades for a neighbouring setting to count; recent_d/recent_min_trades = the most recent window in which the mean excess must still be positive (when it has enough trades), so an edge that has faded drops out of eligibility instead of living on in the long window
_doc.lifecycle: probation_days of live paper-forward evidence; promote_psr probabilistic-Sharpe threshold; CUSUM retire threshold and minimum days; cap on active strategies per stock; min_live_trades = paper trades needed before promotion; cusum_k = CUSUM slack in standard deviations
_doc.calibration: method, minimum resolved forecasts, max expected calibration error, rolling window in days
_doc.forecast: quantile levels, simulated paths, conformal window, tolerance on realised interval coverage
_doc.risk: risk_per_trade_pct of capital; kelly_fraction_cap; max_position_pct; max_sector_pct; max_open_signals; adv_participation_max of average daily volume; drawdown_brake_pct = paper-portfolio drawdown above which new sizes are halved; corr_threshold/corr_size_mult = reduce size for signals highly correlated with one already chosen
_doc.compute: nightly budget in minutes; discovery budget in minutes
_doc.backtest: assumed_order_inr is the reference order size used for the participation check; circuit_proxy_min_move is the smallest |close/prev close - 1| of a one-price day that counts as a circuit-limit lock (no fill)
_doc.signals: entry_atr_mult = half-width of the entry zone in ATRs; stop_atr_min/max/default = allowed range of the volatility stop; swing_low_days = structure-stop lookback; event_window_d = days before a known event that force NO EDGE; plan_horizon_d = horizon of the trade plan simulation; touch_min_prob = a profit level is listed when its touch probability is at least this
_doc.kill: engine/sector/stock is Suspended when live ECE > ece_max (n >= min_n), live interval coverage is off by more than coverage_tol (n >= min_coverage_n), or a CUSUM alarm is active; sector_share = share of a sector's stocks suspended that suspends the sector
_doc.forward_clock_start: first as-of date of the live ledger; journal events dated before it are replays of history (simulation), not live learning, and are tagged as such
_doc.weekly: weekly signal rule, fixed from the weekly study: BUY = best 1% (rank percentile >= buy_top_pct) of liquid stocks by ALADIN 1's 5-day score, SELL = worst 5% (<= sell_bottom_pct); weekly_sd = assumed standard deviation of one weekly trade for the Kelly cap

neutral.bear_note: exit if you hold it, do not add it; a short is possible only through futures

directional.bear_note: exit if you hold it, do not buy it; a short is possible only through futures

disclaimer: ALADIN is a statistical model built by students. It is often wrong. Educational analysis only, not investment advice. Past performance does not predict future results.
